sources.title: cmux README
sources.locator: Overview, setup, features and component boundaries
sources.finding: Mac terminal uses Swift/AppKit and libghostty, CLI/socket automation, attention notifications and scriptable browser panes. cmux ssh connects an existing remote host; Claude Teams supplies provider-owned teammate orchestration.

sources.title: cmux license
sources.locator: Root license grant
sources.finding: The cited root license governs this repository distribution, subject to component notices.

sources.title: cmux iOS
sources.locator: Features; How it works
sources.finding: TestFlight iPhone/iPad client mirrors Mac terminal workspaces over Tailscale or local networking.

sources.title: cmux for Linux
sources.locator: Install; Releases and updates
sources.finding: Linux x64 Chromium/workspace nightly has .run and .deb downloads. It is a distinct client from the Swift Mac terminal.

sources.title: cmux notifications
sources.locator: Quick Start; CLI Usage
sources.finding: Notification panel, native banners, workspace/pane identity and dismissal commands are documented.

sources.title: cmux Cloud
sources.locator: cmux vm new; Cloud in the app
sources.finding: First-party docs describe creating cmux Cloud machines with cmux vm new and listing their workspaces, forwarded ports and terminals in the app. No machine was created in this review.

sources.title: cmux README.md
sources.locator: Session restore; FAQ; skills; licensing
sources.finding: Session snapshots restore layout, directories, best-effort scrollback and browser history, not arbitrary live process checkpoints. Supported agent IDs enable native resume commands. Export/import uses versioned JSON with untrusted-file command restrictions. Remote tmux or persistent Cloud VMs can stay online while the Mac is offline. The terminal works with Gemini CLI, Aider, Cursor Agent, Grok and Pi in addition to Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode.

sources.title: cmux What a machine is; What you need; Quickstart
sources.locator: What a machine is; What you need; Quickstart
sources.finding: Early-access Cloud provides persistent Linux machines whose terminals keep running after panes close, network loss or laptop shutdown. It requires a paid plan, sign-in and Cloud Machines enabled. Machines preserve files/tools, are accessible from any signed-in Mac, and ship Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi.

sources.title: cmux Pricing
sources.locator: Plan cards (Free, Plus, Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise), comparison table and FAQ 'How does billing work?'
sources.finding: Free $0/mo; Plus $15/mo (1 saved Cloud VM); Pro $50/mo or $480/yr; Max $200/mo or $1,920/yr; Team $60/user/mo; Enterprise custom via sales. Paid tiers add Cloud VM capacity, and the terminal plus local agents stay free.

sources.title: cmux Pricing FAQ
sources.locator: FAQ 'Is the terminal really free?' and 'What are Cloud VMs?'
sources.finding: The macOS app is open source and free; local agents run on the user's own API keys at no cost from cmux, and Cloud VMs come only with paid plans.

sources.title: cmux README FAQ, coding agents
sources.locator: README.md lines 404-406 (What coding agents does cmux work with?), commit 94743c7
sources.finding: cmux is a terminal, so any agent CLI that runs in a terminal, such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or Cursor Agent, runs in it unmodified.

sources.locator: web/messages/en.json lines 4992-4999 (docs.cloudSecurity isolation strings, published at cmux.com/docs/cloud-security), commit 94743c7
sources.finding: Each cmux Cloud machine is a microVM with its own Linux kernel rather than a container on a shared kernel; the VM is the security boundary.

sources.title: cmux pricing plans (website source)
sources.locator: web/messages/en.json lines 1821-1850 (pricing free, go/Plus and pro plan feature lists, published on the cmux.com pricing page), commit 94743c7
sources.finding: The $0 Free plan lists the macOS app with no Cloud VMs; the Plus plan includes one saved VM and Pro includes cloud agents on up to five Cloud VMs in isolated remote sandboxes.

sources.finding: User-visible per-workspace checklist items have stable UUIDs, text and pending/in-progress/completed states. The sidebar, CLI and agent control socket can mutate them, and session persistence stores the checklist. This is a per-workspace task checklist, not a full issue backlog.

sources.finding: The public web team implementation defines admin/member roles and permission grants. Team routes re-read membership, require admin or individual permissions, and restrict member promotion/demotion while retaining a last admin.

sources.title: cmux pinned application source
sources.locator: Event-bus subscription, rule matching and executeRun/executeRPC; docs/automations.md
sources.finding: Configured automation rules subscribe to cmux event names such as agent.needs_input and run ordered shell, RPC, notification or outgoing-webhook actions. Rules can act on coding-agent hook events without a human initiating each action; the app process must remain running.

sources.finding: The bundled CLI opens a typed Git diff viewer with selectable source/base, changed files and review/comment handling. The viewer renders proposed changes rather than merely displaying an app preview.

sources.title: cmux pinned application source
sources.locator: Worktree Agents recipe, lines 70-105
sources.finding: The built-in Worktree Agents recipe documents a workspace rooted at a selected Git worktree with side-by-side coding-agent terminals. The chosen worktree must exist; this does not claim automatic provisioning or a security sandbox.

sources.finding: Chief source supplies a product coordinator prompt and dispatch/read/message tools, but the release flag defaults off for everyone, including development builds, unless internal flags or remote PostHog gating enables it.
